comment.body:
Someone, anyone, explain this to me, because it seems not only patently nuts but deliberately misleading, if not fucking fraudulent.

The National Childhood Vaccine INJURY Act (yes, the title of a Congressional Act alone tells you how serious a problem childhood vaccine injuries are) states unequivocally that vaccines fall under Restatement (Second) of Torts §402A, Comment k, titled “Unavoidably unsafe products,” published in 1965 by the American Law Institute, a private organization.

From the Note 4 of the US Supreme Court decision on Bruesewitz v. Wyeth (2011)

//

4 Comment k provides as follows: “Unavoidably unsafe products. There are some products which, in the present state of human knowledge, are quite incapable of being made safe for their intended and ordinary use. These are especially common in the field of drugs. An outstanding example is the vaccine for the Pasteur treatment of rabies, which not uncommonly leads to very serious and damaging consequences when it is injected. Since the disease itself invariably leads to a dreadful death, both the marketing and the use of the vaccine are fully justified, notwithstanding the unavoidable high degree of risk which they involve. Such a product, properly prepared, and accompanied by proper directions and warning, is not defective, nor is it unreasonably dangerous. The same is true of many other drugs, vaccines, and the like, many of which for this very reason cannot legally be sold except to physicians, or under the prescription of a physician. It is also true in particular of many new or experimental drugs as to which, because of lack of time and opportunity for sufficient medical experience, there can be no assurance of safety, or perhaps even of purity of ingredients, but such experience as there is justifies the marketing and use of the drug notwithstanding a medically recognizable risk. The seller of such products, again with the qualification that they are properly prepared and marketed, and proper warning is given, where the situation calls for it, is not to be held to strict liability for unfortunate consequences attending their use, merely because he has undertaken to supply the public with an apparently useful and desirable product, attended with a known but apparently reasonable risk.” Restatement 353–354.

//

So, as early as 1965, this "principle" was formalized PRIVATELY NOT PUBLICLY, then encoded into federal law in the NCVIA (1986), and definitively interpreted by the US Supreme Court in Bruesewitz v. Wyeth (2011) as applying to vaccines as "unavoidably unsafe products".

It's going to take a genius to explain how "unavoidably unsafe" (stated 21 times in the Supreme Court decision) and "unavoidable" side effects (stated 40 times) translate into "safe and effective".

Because they fucking don't, do they?

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1q7S-kGzovICPw8zswJcwwmCrk85CwQ6j/view?usp=sharing

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
//

When you accept a particular ideology as the absolute truth and become so devoted to it that you follow it unquestioningly, your capacity to think reasonably and act responsibly diminishes.

//

Can you explain how closing a matter to question, accepting an idea as true without question, is qualitatively different than:

a. dogmatic belief

b. strong belief

c. any old belief

There are 2 things involved that I find people chronically conflate:

1. The idea

2. The extra magic factor added to the idea to make it a belief

Obviously, a mere idea is not a belief. A mere thought is not a belief. "I think" and "I believe" are not synonymous aside from involving thought/ideas.

So, what is that extra magic factor that makes an idea or a thought into a belief?

I'm not saying that you cannot equate thought = idea = belief. Go ahead if you want to.

I'm saying that in normal usage, people do not mean the same things by those terms.

So, what are actually the real differences between them?

And then, once you've identified that extra magic factor, what does it actually do for you?

And should it do that?

It's called "codependence", and it's easily curable.

A child can, theoretically, reconcile to rapist dads or Munchausen by proxy moms, but there's literally nothing to reconcile when their very world has been ripped to pieces.
